title: Cold Vision
description: Cold vision, the cold vision look, reads the world as temperature: either an arctic photochemical grade with breath and ice, or a thermal false-color overlay with heat edges. Empathy is not in the palette, so pick one sensor and keep it.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Hunts, winter war, a stalker POV: faces become warmer than walls if you are in thermal, or paler than snow if you are in climate. The camera can be lock-off, handheld, or a device POV, but the seeing logic cannot change mid-shot.
Kindness dies in this grade unless the joke is cruelty. It is the wrong tool for a Christmas romance, a beauty key, or a teal wash that only makes skin pale.
If there is no breath, ice, or heat edge, you shot a cool LUT.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Choose one: (1) arctic still, 35mm, breath visible, ice in the air, hard winter sun or overcast white, photochemical blues, or (2) thermal/false-color overlay, readable human hotter than the room, device frame optional but no HUD letters. Do not mix Night Vision green unless that is the device.
Prompt: Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: A hunt through snow, a stalker watching heat, a winter war still. Do not use it as teal-and-sad on a love scene unless cruelty is the point.

Cool Blue is white-balance weather without a seeing-device or ice logic. Cold vision is the named recipe that must pick one of those physics and commit.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Revenant is winter as climate: breath, ice, unkind daylight. The Thing is isolation in cold rooms and a world read as threat.
Name the device if you want a thermal overlay rather than weather.

blocks.text: Name the sensor, then the body. Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat.
Add either breath and ice with a winter key, or false-color heat with a readable face. One logic.
No night-vision green unless you mean that tube.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: A teal grade with pale skin, or a mash of thermal plus Night Vision. The tell is no breath, no ice, no heat edge.
Fix it: pick climate or device, show the physics, hold the face.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Cold Vision in film?
A seeing recipe: arctic climate with breath and ice, or thermal false-color with heat edges. It treats the world as temperature and threat, not as a sad blue LUT.
Cold Vision vs Thermal
Thermal is a specific false-color device look. Cold vision may use that overlay, or it may be photochemical winter. If you want the device, say thermal. If you want climate, show breath and ice.
When should I use Cold Vision?
Hunts, winter war, stalker POV. Skip Christmas romance and any beauty key that only wants pale skin.
How do I prompt Cold Vision for AI image or video?
Pick one sensor. Then: Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat. Add breath and ice, or a heat-edge overlay, and a readable human.
